Subject: OmniFin trial onramp — technical action list & success gates

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the trial running next week:  

1) High-level success criteria (please confirm):  
- Latency: p95 token latency <= 250ms for the user-facing endpoint under target concurrency (50 concurrent users).
- Cost threshold: average per-token cost not to exceed $0.0009 during the trial (we'll track token counts).
- Quality: intent extraction F1 >= 0.86 on your labeled sample set (we'll provide evaluation harness).
- Security/segregation: traffic for trial isolated in VPC peering; logs retained for 30 days.

2) Proposed trial scope and timeline:  
- Day 0 (Nov 16): Access provisioning + trial project created in Redwood console.
- Day 1–3: SDK integration (server-side SDK for streaming).
- Day 4–6: Run smoke tests + baseline eval with your sample prompts.
- Day 7–10: Performance stress tests and model/quantization tuning.

3) Implementation notes (technical):  
- Use our Node SDK (streaming route: POST /v1/generate/stream) for UI streaming.
- For tool calling, we recommend the /v1/chat/call route with tool manifest. We'll share a sample manifest for your backend connectors.
- Prefix caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context to reduce cost; we can preconfigure caches for the 3 top queries you shared.

4) Owners:  
- Redwood tech lead: Grace O'Connor (integration, streaming config).
- Redwood PM/sales: Jonas Weber (trial success, timeline).
- OmniFin lead: Avery Collins (product owner), Ethan Myers (network/security contact).

5) Deliverables we attached: trial_scope.pdf (scope & SLOs), MVP_test_plan.xlsx (test matrix).

Please confirm the success criteria above and any constraints on the timeline (especially the VPC & network window). Once you confirm, Grace will send the integration checklist and a small starter repo with the streaming example.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: OmniFin trial onramp — technical action list & success gates

Thanks Avery — answering inline and attaching a short integration checklist.

- Cost assumption: baseline model = rwd-small (mixed-quant), average session: 120 tokens input + 80 tokens output = 200 tokens/session. At $0.0009/token budget => ~$0.18/session. If you expect higher average lengths we can switch to the rwd-medium variant and re-run the cost projection.

- Network/peering: we only need an egress path to the Redwood private endpoint. For VPC peering during the trial we'll provide a dedicated subnet and temporary egress SG rules. If you want the peering to be created within your maintenance window (Nov 18 08:00–12:00 PT) we can schedule the provisioning then. Please confirm preferred slot.

- Tool manifest & mTLS: attached sample_manifest.json as part of the starter repo. Key points: 1) manifest declares the external tool endpoint + auth type, 2) Redwood will call tool endpoints over mTLS when configured. For now, you can test with token auth in the dev sandbox; we'll enable mTLS for the staging run.

Integration checklist highlights (attached MV):
- API routes: POST /v1/generate/stream (UI streaming, SSE)
- Chat/tool calls: POST /v1/chat/call (supports sync & async tool flows)
- SDKs: Node and Python samples included (server-side streaming + client-side reconnection)
- Metrics hooks: add x-rw-request-id header for traceability; we ingest traces into the console.

Owners and immediate next steps:
- Action: Confirm peering window and token assumptions — Avery (OmniFin).
- Action: Dev sample repo + manifest + network diagram shared — Grace (Redwood) [attached].
- Action: Schedule engineering sync (30 min) after peering scheduled — Dev (Redwood) & OmniFin engineer.

Attachments: MVP_test_plan.xlsx, omnifin_network_diagram.png, starter_repo_link.txt (link to repo and sample manifest).

I'll drop the starter repo link into the thread once I push it.

Thanks,
Grace
